messages.subject: subset option in plotDensity
parts:
Hi anyone (probably Henrik),

I was using the subset option in plotDensity, and I wanted to confirm
that if I say subset=1/2 it doesn't give me a *random* subset of the probes.

I say this because I looked at the code for identifyCells, and this
seems to be how the probes are picked:

if (getFraction) {
indices <- other[seq(from = 1, to = length(other),
by = by)]
}

which means they are equally spaced in the order of the cdf.

I'm not entirely clear on the behavior of 'subset'. If I wanted to give
an vector argument to subset, it should be between 1 and number of Cells
on cdf, right? If I choose type="pm", would it only do the pm ones of
the one I gave to subset, or all (ignoring type="pm')

(By accident, I did subset=1/2 on quantile normalized data and get a set
of arrays (corresponding to a particular batch...) that have fairly
different density plots so I am trying to decide whether that should
worry me)

Best,
Elizabeth

On Feb 8, 2008 12:55 PM, Elizabeth Purdom <epu...@gmail.com> wrote:

> Hi anyone (probably Henrik),
>
> I was using the subset option in plotDensity, and I wanted to confirm
> that if I say subset=1/2 it doesn't give me a *random* subset of the probes.
>
> I say this because I looked at the code for identifyCells, and this
> seems to be how the probes are picked:
>
> if (getFraction) {
> indices <- other[seq(from = 1, to = length(other),
> by = by)]
> }
>
> which means they are equally spaced in the order of the cdf.
>
> I'm not entirely clear on the behavior of 'subset'. If I wanted to give
> an vector argument to subset, it should be between 1 and number of Cells
> on cdf, right? If I choose type="pm", would it only do the pm ones of
> the one I gave to subset, or all (ignoring type="pm')
>
> (By accident, I did subset=1/2 on quantile normalized data and get a set
> of arrays (corresponding to a particular batch...) that have fairly
> different density plots so I am trying to decide whether that should
> worry me)

Yes, you are right that the 'subset' argument is internally passed
down as identifyCells(..., indices=subset) for AffymetrixCdfFile.
Then, the 'indices' argument of identifyCells() is interpreted in
either of two ways. If it is a single numeric value in (0,1) (soft
boundaries), it is interpreted as a fraction, that is, it will return
that fraction of cells. The returned cells are uniformly distributed
from the first to the last cell, as your code snippet shows. If
'indices' is a vector of numeric (or the single value 1), it will be
interpreted exactly as the cells you want.

If you want to get a random subset of a certain fraction of all cells,
you have to generate that yourself and pass it as a vector.

/Henrik
